stories.title: Gardaí 'acted appropriately' prior to M9 crash - Fiosrú
stories.summary: Gardaí "acted appropriately" during their pursuit of a vehicle prior to the fatal crash involving a car driving the wrong way on the M9 in Kildare last month, the office of the police ombudsman, Fiosrú, has found. Five teenage boys died in a head-on collision on the M9 motorway on 16 August. As part of its investigation into the incident, Fiosrú said gardaí had been following the car on the N78 in Athy for a short period before it joined the M9 against the direction of traffic. Four family members in the second car - three women aged in their 20s and 30s and a seven-year-old boy - were seriously injured in the crash and are continuing their recoveries. Fiosrú established that gardaí had pursued a BMW car and permission to continue the pursuit was granted by the garda control room. Other garda units also attempted to place a stopping device at an appropriate location, Fiosrú said.

stories.title: New citizenship rules 'will be difficult for some people'
stories.summary: A 22-year-old man who has received Irish citizenship at a ceremony in Dublin has said new citizenship rules which have been brought to Cabinet "will be difficult for some, but hopefully not too difficult." Adrian Egbukaohia moved to Ireland from Venezuela when he was two years old and applied for citizenship when he became an adult. "I'm about 20 years now waiting for the citizenship," he said. Rules around getting citizenship are set to be tightened under new legislation brought to Cabinet by Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan. They include an increase in the requirement of residency in the country, rising by three years, from five to eight years. A language proficiency test, some knowledge about Irish society and proof of economic self-sufficiency are also expected to become requirements under the new legislation.

stories.title: PBP call for €500 electricity credit and data centre levy
stories.summary: There have been calls in the Dáil for the Government to introduce a €500 electricity credit for every household in Ireland, funded by a new electricity consumption levy on data centres. The Dáil is debating a Private Members' Motion from the Independent and Parties Technical Group, proposed by People Before Profit-Solidarity. People Before Profit TD Richard Boyd Barrett said the measure would "help people who are struggling", as he urged that an additional €500 be given to those with disabilities. "While ordinary people are struggling," he said, "the data centres are paying half the price per unit of electricity", something which he described as "shocking", "disgusting and completely unjustifiable" given their "obscene profits". "Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta - making absolutely obscene profits," the deputy emphasised. Minister for Energy Darragh O'Brien rejected PBP's proposal and tabled a counter-motion, while defending the Government's approach to the cost-of-living crisis.

stories.title: 37 suspected illegal miners die in custody in Nigeria
stories.summary: The governor of a central Nigerian state said 37 people suspected of being illegal miners died while in the custody of the west African country's civil defence corps. Police said they have launched an investigation into the deaths in Niger state, which the civil defence blamed on disease but an intelligence report suggested was due to overcrowding and poor ventilation instead. Niger state - which is more than twice the size of Belgium - is rich in minerals and attracts thousands of artisanal miners, most of them lured by the hope of striking gold. "This morning we woke up to the news that about 37 persons died in the custody of the civil defence here in Minna," Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago told reporters at a news conference in the state capital broadcast by Nigeria's TVC News television. "It's so sad, it's so tragic," he said, adding that a committee of inquiry into the deaths had been set up and had already started work. The governor declared three days of mourning and postponed the start of campaigning for elections due in January.

stories.title: Hallgrimsson cites 'team spirit' amid Israel games unease
stories.summary: Heimir Hallgrimsson says the fact the Republic of Ireland squad have accepted call-ups for the impending UEFA Nations League window is a sign of "team spirit" as he acknowledged that some individual players' are "uncomfortable" about the prospect of playing against Israel. Ireland open their Nations League campaign next Thursday against Kosovo in Pristina, while they will also host Austria at Aviva Stadium on 1 October in the third match of the extended four-game international window. But since the Nations League draw was made in February, controversy has surrounded the two fixtures against Israel which will take place either side of the Austria match. Ireland's 'away' game against the Israelis will take place on neutral ground in Debrecen, Hungary next Sunday, 27 September. A week later, the designated Irish 'home' match will be staged in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October. However, calls for a boycott of the games have abounded amid the backdrop of ongoing events in Gaza. Last September, an independent UN commission concluded that Israel has committed and continues to commit genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Israeli authorities rejected the findings of the report.

stories.summary:
Eamon O'Shea and Ger Manley will head up the management teams for the 2026 shinty-hurling/camogie internationals. Male and female sides will take on their Scottish counterparts in the hybrid sport, in a double-header at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh on Saturday, 24 October. The women's shinty-camogie international will begin at 4pm, before the men’s shinty-hurling clash takes place at 6pm. Manley, who guided Cork to All-Ireland senior camogie glory in August, will manage the women's team. The Inniscarra native, who previously represented Ireland as a player, also steered the camogie team to victory in Inverness in 2025. His management team comprises: Gemma O’Connor, Elaine Dowds,
Jennifer Mehigan, Kieran McCarthy and Pat O’Neill.

stories.title: English FA calls for independent review of FIFA plan
stories.summary: English Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has written to FIFA president Gianni Infantino calling for an independent review into the World Cup private investor plan and the handling of the Folarin Balogun case, the Press Association understands. Infantino is under pressure after three continental confederations rejected his plan to create a company to run the commercial aspects of FIFA's tournament such as the men’s and women’s World Cups and sell 20% of it to private investors. The Times was first to report on Thursday that FA chair Hewitt, who is also a FIFA vice-president and a member of the FIFA Council, had written to Infantino demanding answers. The Press Association understands the letter calls for an independent review of the private investor proposal, and for clarity around the decision by FIFA’s disciplinary committee to suspend a one-match ban for United States striker Balogun during the World Cup. The suspension of Balogun’s ban was followed by an admission from US President Donald Trump that he had called Infantino asking for the red card shown to the striker against Bosnia and Herzegovina to be reviewed. Infantino apologised over the process followed in regard to the private investor plan on 5 August, and a statement from FIFA’s management board pledged there would be a review. FIFA has not at any stage confirmed who is undertaking that review.

stories.title: Munster pair keen to show provincial form in Irish green
stories.summary: If team sheets were named on form alone, Munster would dominate Scott Bemand's thoughts following their interprovincial title success last month. Having now picked off eight wins on the bounce across the past two campaigns, with an average winning margin of 29 points; they are not shorn of talent bursting through the seams. Two players likely to get the chance to show their provincial form on a national level are forwards Jane Clohessy and Beth Buttimer. Heading into the autumn test window, the UL Bohemians team-mates have just one cap between them, but that looks destined to change in the coming weeks and months. For Clohessy, who made her Ireland debut in the 2025 Six Nations defeat to Scotland, it has been a rocky road back to contention. The daughter of Munster legend Peter, she missed out on selection for the Rugby World Cup later that year, and suffered two separate arm breaks during the Celtic Challenge, and again in Ireland training, to miss out on Six Nations game time. But she's back and in tip-top form, so much so that missed the interprovincial final win over Leinster is easily glossed over.

stories.title: Mr. Hayes is now entombed: Maeve Higgins digs into RTÉ's Archives
stories.summary: Many years ago, myself and my sister Lilly were part of the best TV show ever made in Ireland, and possibly in the world. It's called Fancy Vittles and you can find it on the dark web. The editor, Ian Cudmore, and myself watched loads of RTE archival footage for it. The clip that stays with me is from 1968, where a man named Tim Hayes gets buried alive in Cobh. A show called Newsbeat captures the moment he is dug back up having successfully broken the record for time spent buried alive. We watched this short piece repeatedly because it's both funny and melancholy - an irresistible combination. The footage is impossibly different to anything filmed today; black and white, odd angles, awkward cuts. There is a strange loop of audio that doesn’t quite match what we see. There are thousands of people gazing with excitement at a pipe sticking out of the ground. Hayes’s mother Marguerite speaks directly into the camera, she is emotional, almost melodramatic. The journalist, Bill O’Herlihy, adopts a jaunty tone, one that jars with the dark undertones of such a happening.

stories.title: Late Late reveals guests for first show of new season
stories.summary: Announcing Friday's guests, The Late Late Show said: "Siobhán McSweeney will discuss the runaway success of The Traitors Ireland. She'll tell Patrick why she rules the castle with an iron fist as Lady Muck and how she celebrated winning her first BAFTA. She'll also be joined in studio by some of the banished and murdered players from this year's series as anticipation for next week's final grows. "The stars of the biggest sports story this summer will be live in studio, still riding the green and red wave! Members of the Mayo team and manager Andy Moran will share what life has been like since the All-Ireland victory that got the country, and the world, talking. "Star player and GAA wunderkind Kobe McDonald is back from Australia, where buzz is building around him as the most exciting new talent in Aussie Rules, while Mayo stalwart and fan favourite Aidan O'Shea will reflect on what the win meant for him after a decade and a half of ferociously battling for Sam. "Irish star Caitríona Balfe will join Patrick to chat about her role in Sense and Sensibility - a new take on Jane Austen's iconic story of love and sisterhood. The Monaghan actress will chat about her attraction to period drama and bonding with her co-stars Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles. She'll also talk about saying goodbye to Outlander this year after eight epic seasons and why filming Kenneth Branagh's Belfast is still one of her proudest experiences. "Actor Liam Neeson and historian Catherine Corless will be in studio to tell Patrick about their new film, The Lost Children of Tuam. Liam, who is one of the producers of the film, will talk about why Catherine's story had to be heard and Catherine will discuss how the fight for the truth is still ongoing. "Following the success of their chart-topping, record-breaking album The User's Guide to Being Human, The Script will drop into studio for some live music and a chat. Danny O'Donoghue will talk about how married life is treating him, how he continues to honour Mark Sheehan's memory through music, and what fans can expect as the band prepare to head out on the road in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Star-studded campaign kicks off Irish Fashion Week 2026
stories.summary: Last night at the 3Arena's Studio, Ireland's movers and shakers gathered to celebrate the return of Ireland Fashion Week (7–12 October 2026). Under the theme of 'Coming Home: An Island in Motion', the celebrations began with the release of a new campaign, which brought together eight leading figures from Irish film, music, fashion, sport and culture against the extraordinary Atlantic landscape of Roundstone, Connemara. Photographed by internationally acclaimed Irish photographer Damian Foxe, the creative project launches the countdown to Ireland Fashion Week, which returns with eight shows and more than 90 designers. The launch features actor Jamie-Lee O’Donnell; racing driver Max Hart; Irish fashion icon Celia Holman Lee; Ireland Fashion Week Model of the Year Marwa Noelle Ali; musicians Travy and Abdu Huss, known as KhakiKid; digital creator Lauren Whelan; and actor and model Ivana Miličević. Speaking on the theme of the shoot, Ashley McDonnell, Founder of Ireland Fashion Week, says: "We wouldn't have been able to pull off last year without all the people that came - sometimes with 10, 20, 30 years of experience abroad - home, and you can really see that in this campaign." Speaking further on the theme, Ashley said: "We wanted this to feel both familiar and unexpected. To capture the Ireland we know and love while showing the confidence, diversity and creative energy shaping the country today.

stories.title: Man, 50s, due in court charged over Healy-Rae assault
stories.summary: A man is due in court this morning charged in connection with the assault on Kerry TD Michael Healy-Rae. The man, aged in his 50s, is due to appear before a sitting of Dublin District Court at around 10.30am. Mr Healy-Rae was travelling in his own vehicle on Cork Street in Dublin city at around 4.10pm on Wednesday when he was approached by a man who assaulted him through the window of his car. Following the assault, the Kerry TD was taken from the road by gardaí who were quickly on the scene. They took him to Kevin Street Garda Station and an ambulance was called. He attended St Vincent's University Hospital for his injuries, and was discharged around 9pm on Wednesday night, having needed stitches for injuries to his face and mouth.

stories.summary: The minimum cost of building a metro for Dublin has more than doubled in four years, with the estimated price tag now between €14.4bn and €17.5bn. The Government has approved the revised cost of MetroLink, allowing the project to fully go to tender, with a view to works beginning next year. It is one of the most significant milestones in the history of the project, which was first announced more than 25 years ago. When the Government applied for planning permission for MetroLink in 2022, it said the predicted price tag was around €9.5bn, based on a range of between €7.16bn and €12.25bn The new estimated cost now ranges from €14.4bn to €17.5bn with the expected centre point of €15.75bn. MetroLink says that building inflation and design changes have led to the increased bill.

stories.title: Fall in job postings but hiring demand steadying - Indeed
stories.summary: The number of job postings on hiring platform Indeed has fallen by 9.1% on an annual basis but has recorded a monthly increase of 2.7%. According to its latest Labour Market Snapshot, Indeed said that overall hiring demand has steadied in recent months, with job postings sitting broadly at their early-2020 pre-pandemic baseline. The report found that despite modest softening, the labour market remains close to full employment, with the unemployment rate remaining at 5%. "The figures illustrate a labour market that has normalised following a period of persistently elevated labour demand post-pandemic," Indeed said. According to the research, the share of Irish job postings that mention AI terms in the description continues to rise rapidly and is now at 14.7% of all postings. This is the highest among European countries tracked by Indeed.

stories.title: Left-wing bloc wins slim majority in Swedish election
stories.summary: Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson will resign after losing the country's parliamentary election, he said following the announcement of a final vote count. Centre-left opposition parties won 176 seats in Sunday's vote for parliament while Kristersson's ruling right-wing bloc secured 173 seats, the election authority said earlier as the counting of ballots ended. "Now it is the speaker who will lead the next stage of the way to a new government. I am herewith requesting that I be relieved of the office of prime minister to allow that work to start immediately," Mr Kristersson said in a letter posted on social media X. The four parties in the left-wing bloc, led by Magdalena Andersson's Social Democrats, hold a slim majority in the 349-seat parliament over outgoing prime minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing alliance, which includes the anti-immigration Sweden Democrats. But only around 50,000 votes separated the two sides in the country of 10.6 million people. Ms Andersson vowed today to lead the country in a "new direction" after four years of right-wing rule backed by the far-right.

stories.title: Hoops are vulnerable but have enough to get over line
stories.summary: There are bad runs of form and then there are bad runs of form at the wrong time. The champions have now gone seven games without a win in all competitions. Their last victory came against Dundalk on the 7 August - six weeks ago by the time they face Waterford tonight. When you look at the form of the three teams involved in this title race the contrast is obvious. Over the last five league games St Patrick's Athletic have taken 12 points, Bohemians 10 and Rovers just six. That would be unusual enough for a side that has dominated Irish football for the best part of six years. The timing is what makes it worrying. Historically this has been the period when Stephen Bradley’s Rovers tend to gather speed. European football is either finished or settling down, the squad has found its rhythm and the experience within the dressing room begins to tell. They have made a habit of starting seasons slowly, often following shortened pre-seasons because of European commitments, before eventually building momentum that becomes very difficult to stop.

stories.title: Cahill reveals new Tipp management team for 2027
stories.summary: All-Ireland SHC winning manager Liam Cahill will work with a much-changed backroom team for the 2027 season. In July it was announced that Cahill – who guided the Premier County to the Liam MacCarthy in 2025 – was to remain in place until 2029. Their title defence didn't go to plan with the side failing to get out of Munster last season and it will be a changed management team hoping to make amends next year. Selectors Declan Laffan and TJ Ryan depart with Brian O'Meara and Sean O'Meara in place. Paul O'Brien will be a selector and offer coaching support with Aidan Stakelum also acting in a coaching support role. Angelo Walsh also leaves and strength and conditioning coach position with Kilkenny man John Murphy now taking on that role. Diarmuid Cahill, who recently stepped down as Longford boss, will be goalkeeping coach with Anne Marie Kennedy overseeing sports performance.

stories.title: McDonnell and Gill earn first Ireland U21s call-ups
stories.summary: Nottingham Forest midfielder Grady McDonnell and Celtic goalkeeper Marcus Gill have been named in the Republic of Ireland's Under-21s squad for first time ahead of the European Championship qualifiers against Slovakia, Kazakhstan and England. McDonnell was a key part of the Ireland Under-17s side that made it to the last 16 of the FIFA World Cup last November. Scotland-born Gill has been capped up to Under-19 level, and recently went on loan to Scottish League One side East Kilbride. stories.title: Cantwell excited by 'massive' PWR merger opportunity
stories.summary: The IRFU is expected to discover if its bid to join Premiership Women's Rugby is successful in the next three to four months, with a potential merger for the 2028/29 season on the cards. Lynne Cantwell, Irish Rugby’s head of women’s strategy, says they are focused on exploring the "massive" opportunity to merge the Celtic Challenge with what she describes as the "best elite domestic league in the world". In April, PWR welcomed expressions of interest for expanding the current nine-team English league, with the IRFU making a combined bid along with the Welsh and Scottish unions, which could see the Celtic Challenge merge to form a British and Irish League. "We're on that journey. The opportunity to play in a cross-border competition with the Red Roses and the Scottish players and Welsh players is really significant, so it's one we are very focused on exploring. "It's the best elite domestic league in the world at the moment. What we are seeing is a lot of international players to play in the English league because of that." If successful, the earliest timeline for a potential merger of the leagues would likely be in the 2028/29 season, but Cantwell explained there is a lot of red tape to be crossed before anything is confirmed.

stories.title: The Cult Of Sharing: D.A.D.D.Y. welcome you to Culture Night 2026
stories.summary: Living in Dublin twenty-ish years ago, when the first Culture Nights arrived, there was a lovely luminous energy in the newness of it. One of the first years, we made a beeline for the Grand Lodge of Ireland, a Kubrick-coded Freemasons' Hall on Molesworth Street. It’s a venue now, but back then it had been shrouded in mystery. People hadn’t really been in there before. The building is almost absurdly rich in symbolism, and on that first visit, the esoteric, cinematic beauty of it didn’t disappoint. So for us, that first Culture Night experience started by being nosy, sharing the moment of being behind the curtain with a bunch of friends and fellow weirdos into this strange new place. Part private members’ club, part church, part B-movie. Watch the trailer for D.A.D.D.Y.'s feature film Extra Ordinary And so, in order to honour that memory, today we’re getting our own guild of members together, and peeping behind the weird curtain of memory and culture. Like the Freemasons, we meet regularly, share traditions and rituals, look out for one another and have a strong sense of belonging. Mostly on WhatsApp now, but you get the idea. Have you seen this? You’d like this. Or this. Or them. Wait until you see it! Isn’t this terrible?

stories.title: Macklemore praises Ms Rachel's $1m Gaza aid donation
stories.summary: US rapper Macklemore has praised children's YouTuber Ms Rachel as she pledges to match his donation of $1 million (€872,000) - to charities supporting Palestinian people. The musician announced on Wednesday he would be donating his entire net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour after being dropped as a supporting act over comments he made about Gaza. Since then, all of Sheeran’s Loop Tour supporting acts, including Irish singer Aaron Rowe, Grammy award-winning musician Finneas, who is Billie Eilish’s brother, and Danish singer Lukas Graham, as well as his backing band Beoga, have dropped out of the remaining dates. US YouTube star Ms Rachel, real name Rachel Anne Accurso, shared a post to Instagram on Thursday as she revealed she is following Macklemore’s lead and also donating to pro-Palestinian charities. The children’s entertainer, 43, wrote: "I will match Macklemore’s donation and I invite every wealthy white celebrity to match it and speak out against the genocide in Gaza. "Over 20,000 precious Palestinian children have been killed and children continue to be killed every day.

stories.title: 5 trending watch styles to try – including smartwatches
stories.summary: Wearing a watch almost became obsolete when we all started using our mobile phones to tell the time, but now timepieces are being used as wearable jewellery again. That means a host of whole new watch trends are sweeping fashion – from the red carpet to the streets, and even the gym. From tiny timepieces to maximalist faces, there are a lot of trendy watches to love – and while high-end models can go for eye-watering prices, it’s perfectly achievable to get similar looks for a whole lot less. Here are some of the key watch trends to add to your jewellery collection. "Big timepieces have officially been replaced with dainty tiny watches that blur the lines between a watch and a bracelet," says Natasha Cooper, a retail and trend expert at MediaVision, who has five years’ experience working in the retail space, with a focus on fashion, jewellery and watch trends. "Watches have moved from its objective to tell the time and have now become a fashion statement and something that can be seamlessly intertwined with your bracelet stack."

stories.title: Burnham meeting a chance to 'inject momentum' - Taoiseach
stories.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin said his meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is an opportunity to "inject further momentum" into the partnership between the two governments. The Taoiseach is meeting Mr Burnham in Manchester - becoming the first international leader to visit Number 10 North, the new North of England outpost of Downing Street. As well as British-Irish bilateral issues like trade, the two leaders will discuss Northern Ireland, the planned EU-UK summit in November, and international issues ahead of next weeks UN General Assembly. It is their first meeting since Mr Burnham became prime minster - but the two have met several times previously, particularly when Mr Burnham was Mayor of Greater Manchester and led trade delegations to Ireland. Mr Burnham said: "I'm delighted to be hosting the Taoiseach as the first international leader to visit No 10 North - this is a historic moment and a proud day for Manchester. "No 10 North is all about creating opportunities for working people, and our partnership with Ireland as we improve the lives of people in both of our countries is a key part of that.

stories.title: School absence up among disadvantaged students - study
stories.summary: School absence has increased among young people with socio-emotional difficulties and those who do not like school in the last 10 years, research has shown. New research, published by the ESRI and produced in partnership with Tusla, uses Growing Up in Ireland (GUI) data to trace patterns of absence from nine to 13 years of age, identifying the individual, family and school factors that contribute to school absence. Among the key findings were that absence rates vary significantly by social background, with higher rates among unskilled manual and non-employed families, those whose mothers have lower levels of education, families experiencing financial strain and lone-parent households. It also stated that national data revealed higher rates of school absence in Ireland since the pandemic, as has been found in many other countries. It further found that young people with a disability are much more likely to miss school than their peers. Young people for whom a disability emerged or was identified between nine and 13 years tend to have increasing absence rates.

stories.title: Government must make 'trade offs' for Budget - Chambers
stories.summary: Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers is to warn his Cabinet colleagues that they will have to make trade offs as the Government moves to moderate spending in Budget 2027 amid global uncertainty over the war in Iran. Ahead of next month's budget announcement, Mr Chambers is expected to tell ministers that they must "prioritise and make choices and trade offs for 2027". He will say expenditure will increase by €7 billion next year, representing a 6% increase on 2025, but still a moderation on the spending increases of recent years. The reminder for his fellow ministers comes with budget preparations intensifying as the Dáil resumes from its summer break later today. It is unclear how the warning will be received by ministers amid some friction earlier this year when the Fianna Fáil deputy leader announced spending curbs and introduced levies for each department to pay for cost overruns in the Department of Education. The move comes as the Coalition mulls on whether to extend excise cuts on petrol and diesel due to be unwound from 1 November.

stories.title: Stripe to provide payments platform for BT Arnotts group
stories.summary: Department store group Brown Thomas Arnotts has announced a new partnership with financial technology company Stripe. Under the deal, the retailer will move online payments processing for its Brown Thomas and Arnotts websites and mobile apps to Stripe. "Stripe's technology and pace of innovation have enabled Brown Thomas Arnotts to continually innovate and deliver the effortless, elevated experience our customers expect, wherever and however they choose to shop," said Sarah Esler, Head of Digital Product, Brown Thomas Arnotts. Conor McNamara, Chief Revenue Officer for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at Stripe, said its features like Authorization Boost and Radar have helped businesses recover revenue from card declines. "We expect the same for Brown Thomas Arnotts as they migrate their entire online payments volume to Stripe," Mr McNamara. Stripe was founded by Irish brothers Patrick and John Collison.

stories.title: US passes sanctions bill targeting Russia
stories.summary: The US House of Representatives has passed a sweeping sanctions and tariff bill intended to increase economic pressure on Russia. US President Donald Trump will sign the legislation into law nearly one-and-a-half years after the late Senator Lindsey Graham introduced it. The bill, now called the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' to honour the South Carolina Republican, passed the Senate last month. The House passed voted 262 to 159 in favour, as dozens of Democrats broke with party leaders to join the majority of Republicans. The new measures target Russia's energy and defence industries, as well as its ‘shadow fleet’ of tankers that evade existing sanctions. The bill faced opposition as it also authorises President Trump to impose stiff tariffs on China, India and other countries to reduce their dependence on Russian oil and gas, as well as to extend sanctions on Iran.

stories.title: Mayo and Kerry confirm All-Ireland rematch in London
stories.summary: Kerry GAA and Mayo GAA have confirmed that they will face off in an exhibition game in London this coming November. Dubbed the 'JRL Group Presents the Mayo Kerry Global Series', the news follows approval from the GAA Central Council for the All Ireland final repeat. The clash will take place on Saturday 28 November at the StoneX Stadium in Barnet, home of Premiership rugby outfit Saracens. The sides famously met in the 2026 All-Ireland final as Andy Moran's green and red ended 75 years of pain to finally lift Sam Maguire. The game will also see Mayo return to England for the second time this year, having defeated London in the early rounds of the Connacht Championship.
